limitations: The stored ions are measured alternately under the same trap voltages, using separate axial resonators. Randomized species order reduces linear drift; it does not make sequential measurements simultaneous or statistically independent.
The proton dataset comprises thirteen runs and three ion pairs, with about 300 hours of acquisition over two months. Runs, cycles, ion pairs and publications are not independent replications.
The planar fit extrapolates the deliberately excited cyclotron motion to zero using R_i=R_stat+a*S_p^2+b*S_C^2. Thermal axial and cyclotron motion still requires systematic corrections.
The 2019 reanalysis corrects the estimated ion temperatures and a minor measurement-program flaw in the 2017 datasets. The two publications cannot be averaged as independent proton-mass experiments.

Heiße 2017 Figure 3 lists phase-unwrapping times 0.1, 1, 2 and 5 s; Heiße 2019 describes 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 s. The four final 10 s phase evolutions are distinct from those unwrapping stages; the differing descriptions are retained.

The 2017 abbreviation MT denotes the measurement trap; in 2019 PT denotes the precision trap and MT the magnetometer trap. The proposed simultaneous three-ion readout and magnetic shim coils were not used in the reported proton campaign.

The proton campaign had C4=(0 +/- 6.3)e-6 and C6=(-6.8 +/- 0.4)e-4. The improved Table VI tuning and proposed millikelvin cooling describe other conditions, not the acquisition used for the reported mass.

Heiße 2019 Table VIII reports corrections in parts per trillion: image charge 91.0(4.6), image current -1.9(0.3), line shape 3.1(3.0), magnetron determination 0.0(0.6), magnetic inhomogeneity -20.9(27.4), relativity -8.9(7.1), and electrostatic terms much smaller than 0.1. Its total is 59.5(28.8).

Adding all finite displayed rows gives 62.4 ppt. The line-shape correction varies by ion pair; the 2017 Table I caption explicitly excludes its pair-specific term from that earlier total. Omitting the 2019 line-shape row gives 59.3 ppt. The final weighting and application to the reanalysis have not been reconstructed; a naive sum is not evidence that the mass result is invalid.

The 2019 Table VIII header is (R_stat-R_cor)/R_stat, but Equations 20 and 23 increase R, giving (R_cor-R_stat)/R_stat about +59.55 ppt from rounded values. The printed sign convention remains unresolved.

Table VII revises feedback-cooled axial temperatures to 1.5(1.0) K for p and 4.5(1.4) K for C-12(6+), replacing the 2017 common 1.7(1.0) K estimate. No-feedback values are 3.4(1.0) K and 6.4(1.0) K. These are inferred temperatures, not zero thermal energies.
The reanalysis uses B2=-0.270(15) microtesla/mm^2. Reduced chi-square 1.17 for ten degrees of freedom and a 30 percent tail do not logically exclude common systematic effects.

Heiße 2019 Equation 21 prints a frequency shift with a dimensionless right side; the relative form in Heiße 2017 Equation 2 and the explicit conventions in Schuh 2019 are used instead. The positive E/(m*c^2) beside a negative relativistic shift on page 13 is not adopted as a physical identity.
For positive deuteron binding energy, m_n=m_d-m_p+E_B/c^2. The subtraction wording on Heiße 2019 page 14 is not an independent neutron-mass determination or a replacement for that mass balance.

Neutral carbon-12 has mass exactly 12 u; C-12(6+) instead has mass 12 u minus six electron masses plus the six positive ionization energies divided by c^2. The sixfold charge factor in m_p=R*m_C/6 cannot be omitted.

Heiße 2019 uses m_e=0.000548579909069(15) u and historical electronic-energy inputs. The electron mass is inferred using a bound-electron g factor and QED; it is not an independently reproduced direct weighing in this review.

Heiße 2017 prints m_C=11.9967096264139(10) u and 0.08 ppt relative uncertainty. Heiße 2019 prints 11.99670962641385(8) u but still states 0.08 ppt; the printed (8) corresponds to about 0.00667 ppt. This unresolved uncertainty discrepancy is not silently repaired.

The proton-electron ratio in Heiße 2019 assumes zero covariance because the dominant proton and electron systematic uncertainties differ. That assumption is not proof of complete statistical independence.
These are reported measurements or calculations with scoped interpretations. Original acquisition records, analysis code, thermal corrections and full covariance have not been independently replayed.

A bare proton, a charged carbon or oxygen nucleus, and a neutral atom have different masses and charge factors. These mass results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal carrier minimum.
The quoted CODATA 2014 and AME 2016 comparisons are historical reference values. They are not current recommended constants or independent experiments reconstructed by this review.

records.description: For the selected ambient-water structure analysis, the oxygen-oxygen pair-distribution function g_OO(r) describes a radial spatial correlation of oxygen positions. A distance-shell coordination is an integral of 4*pi*rho_O*r^2*g_OO(r) over stated radial bounds. It is distinct from a unique angular hydrogen-bond network, cluster identity or time correlation. In the selected dynamics model, C_n(t)=average P_n[u_OH(0) dot u_OH(t)] characterizes orientational decorrelation, while a completed hydrogen-bond partner exchange uses its own state definition and endpoint conditions. Static pair structure, orientational relaxation, exchange waiting time, angular-event duration and molecular persistence are different quantities.

records.description: The selected ambient-water X-ray reanalysis supports finite ensemble-averaged radial oxygen shell structure under the reported conditions. A separate rigid-SPC/E simulation and jump/frame model supports a specified picture of hydrogen-bond acceptor exchange and orientational reconfiguration with distinct correlation time scales. Together these provide bounded positive structural and dynamical descriptions of a liquid, while retaining the distinction between measured-derived spatial correlations and computational trajectories. They establish neither universal self-organization, uniquely observed networks, obligatory crystal precursors nor necessary dispersion/hydrogen-bond/dipole fractions for all liquids.
records.name: Scoped liquid-water structure and dynamical-organization evidence
openObligations: The positive scope is ambient-water spatial statistics plus a separately supplied finite model of liquid-water reorientation. Spatial statistics can coexist with changing neighbors. Persistence of an equilibrium distribution is an additional modelling statement, not a measured neighbor or network lifetime.

Original fluctuating clusters, network-like correlations and continuously reconfiguring constraints are narrowed: radial pair data do not uniquely identify a network or cluster, and the trajectory mechanism depends on the supplied geometric/model definitions.
Equilibrium statistical correlation does not by itself prove a driven nonequilibrium self-organization mechanism, universal collective coordination law or a new stable bounded entity.

The selected liquid does not require prior crystallization. There is no necessary crystal-to-liquid causal stage or universal position between isolated motion and crystalline order derived from these two publications.

Viscosity, surface tension, dielectric response and cooperative transport are original proposed consequences. They are not measured or quantitatively derived by the selected reanalysis and reorientation model. Referenced prior relaxation experiments are not imported as newly reviewed studies.

Original necessary parents 2.6 dispersion, 2.7 hydrogen bonds and 2.8 molecular polarization are relevant descriptions for particular liquids, not universal prerequisites proven here. The selected SPC/E model does not estimate their independent causal fractions or prove that every liquid is polar or hydrogen bonded.
Original weights 0.4/0.35/0.25, directions [2], modes [0,1]/[0,1]/[1], dependency type 10 and arising roles remain catalogue provenance without an admitted causal estimator or universal necessity.

Original carrier group 1/type 0, all N_min=N_crit=3 and null N_sat are catalogue defaults. The coordination integral, three-body switch illustration and finite 256-molecule simulation do not establish a universal three-molecule threshold, three hydrogen bonds or a minimum cluster lifetime.

Original Level 2, Phase 2, TypeRole 2, Science [1,2], established, MustCover [10], ShouldCover [9] and Optional [] are ontology/display choices. The SOMA higher-order pattern label is not an independently measured physical carrier or an additional causal law.

Generic statistical-mechanics/MD and scattering/spectroscopy/viscosity/diffusion/dynamic-structure evidence placeholders are replaced only by the actually read structural reanalysis and computational model. No separate dynamic-structure-factor experiment, spectroscopy acquisition or bulk transport measurement is invented.
The two publications do not share a newly fitted model or jointly validate one unique network. The 2006 dynamics model was not calibrated against the later 2013 benchmark in this reconstruction.

No new acquisition, full underlying-paper review, auxiliary-data download, raw-data refit, diffraction/window replay, molecular-dynamics execution, lifetime distribution, force-field fit or independent empirical reproduction is claimed.
